title: Building Energy Efficiency Disclosure Amendment Bill 2014
short_title: Building Energy Efficiency Disclosure Amendment Bill 2014

speeches.speaker: Bob Baldwin
speeches.brief: Moved the Building Energy Efficiency Disclosure Amendment Bill to streamline the Commercial Building Disclosure Program, which began in November 2011, by easing certificate and exemption requirements for building owners, estimating the changes would cut $600,000 worth of regulatory burden on businesses.

speeches.speaker: Gary Gray
speeches.brief: Supported the Building Energy Efficiency Disclosure Amendment Bill, noted the commercial building sector accounts for around 10 per cent of Australia's greenhouse gas emissions, and flagged concern about a government-commissioned review of the Commercial Building Disclosure program due by March 2015 that could see the program scrapped.

speeches.speaker: Alex Hawke
speeches.brief: Supported amendments to the Building Energy Efficiency Disclosure Act, saying exemptions for building owners who receive unsolicited sale offers would reduce regulatory costs by about $300,000, and said the bill overall would cut close to $600,000 in regulatory burden on business.

speeches.speaker: Steve Irons
speeches.brief: Explained that the bill would streamline the Commercial Building Disclosure scheme by addressing unsolicited offers, subsidiary transactions, assessor accreditation, certificate commencement dates, exemptions and online guidance, while noting that an independent review would report by March 2015.

speeches.speaker: Sharon Claydon
speeches.brief: Supported the bill as a stakeholder-backed housekeeping measure, arguing that energy efficiency can reduce emissions and costs, citing research and projects in Newcastle, and warning that the program review should not become a pretext for abolition.

speeches.speaker: Nickolas Varvaris
speeches.brief: Supported the bill's aim of reducing red tape in the Commercial Building Disclosure scheme, including exemptions for unsolicited offers and wholly-owned subsidiaries, clearer assessor functions, flexible certificate dates, simpler exemptions and online guidance.

speeches.speaker: Graham Perrett
speeches.brief: Commended the member for Barton and restated a commitment to repay a debt involving a beer.

speeches.speaker: Craig Kelly
speeches.brief: Supported amendments to building energy efficiency disclosure laws, arguing that scrapping the Renewable Energy Target would avoid wasting $17 billion given compact fluorescent bulbs already release more mercury into landfill nationally than coal power stations do, and credited the carbon tax repeal with the biggest fall in electricity prices in the nation's history.

speeches.speaker: Keith Pitt
speeches.brief: Supported amendments streamlining building energy efficiency disclosure rules, noting energy efficient lamps cost between $6 and $11 compared with about $1 for old incandescent bulbs, and cited a National Electricity Market report finding Australia has enough generating capacity for the next decade, with usage falling and supply exceeding demand by 135 per cent.

speeches.speaker: Bob Baldwin
speeches.brief: Reported that the Building Energy Efficiency Disclosure Amendment Bill 2014 would streamline the Commercial Building Disclosure Program, remove assessments for certain transactions, allow later certificate commencement dates, and produce regulatory savings of around $600,000 annually.

acts.title: Building Energy Efficiency Disclosure Amendment Act 2015
